</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Mass is the amount of matter in an object
The SI units of weight and mass are the same

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass is the amount of matter in an object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is defined as the fundamental measure of the **amount of matter** contained within an object. It is an intrinsic property that does not change regardless of the object's position in the universe. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Weight** is the force exerted on an object due to **gravity**. It is calculated using the formula **W = m × g**, where 'm' is mass and 'g' is the acceleration due to gravity. Therefore, weight is directly dependent on the gravitational pull of the location. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **SI unit of mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**, while the **SI unit of weight** is the **Newton (N)** because weight is a measure of force. Since they represent different physical quantities, their units are not the same. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **mass** of an object remains **constant** throughout the universe unless matter is physically added to or removed from the object. It does not fluctuate based on altitude, latitude, or different celestial bodies. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• While **mass** is a **scalar quantity** (having only magnitude), **weight** is a **vector quantity** because it has both magnitude and a direction pointing towards the center of gravity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Variations:**
 
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** on **Earth** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. However, on the **Moon**, gravity is about **1/6th** of that on Earth.
 
• Consequently, an object with a **mass** of **60 kg** will have a weight of **588 N** on Earth but only about **98 N** on the Moon, even though its **mass** remains exactly **60 kg**.
 
 
 
• **Measurement Tools:**
 
 
• **Mass** is typically measured using a **physical balance** or a **beam balance**, which compares an unknown mass with a known standard mass.
 
• **Weight** is measured using a **spring balance**, which measures the extension of a spring caused by the gravitational pull on the object.
 
 
 
• **Inertia:**
 
 
• **Mass** is also a measure of **inertia**, which is the resistance of an object to any change in its state of motion. The greater the **mass**, the higher the **inertia**, making it harder to accelerate or stop the object.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Center of Gravity:** This is the point through which the entire **weight** of a body acts. For a regular-shaped object with uniform density, this point usually coincides with its geometric center.
 
• **Zero Weight:** An object can experience **weightlessness** (zero weight) in **free fall** or in **deep space** far from any celestial body, but its **mass** can never be **zero** as long as it exists as matter.
 
• **Relativistic Mass:** According to **Albert Einstein's** theory of relativity, the **mass** of an object can appear to increase when it travels at speeds approaching the **speed of light**, though for all general science and classical mechanics applications, mass is considered **constant**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the purpose of anodising aluminium metals?

options.text: To make it more reactive with air
To form a protective oxide layer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To form a protective oxide layer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anodising** is a sophisticated **electrolytic process** used to increase the thickness of the natural **oxide layer** on the surface of metal parts, most commonly **aluminium**.
 
• During this process, a clean **aluminium** article is made the **anode** in an electrolytic bath, usually containing an acid such as **dilute sulphuric acid**.
 
• When an electric current is passed through the electrolyte, **oxygen gas** is evolved at the **anode**, which reacts with the **aluminium** to form a thick, uniform, and **protective layer of aluminium oxide (Al2O3)**.
 
• The primary objective of this process is to provide **corrosion resistance** and enhance the **durability** of the metal by creating a barrier against environmental factors. ***Hence, the correct answer is to form a protective oxide layer.***
 
• Unlike paint or plating, this **oxide layer** is fully integrated with the underlying **aluminium** substrate, so it cannot chip or peel off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aesthetic and Decorative Uses**:
 
 
• The **anodic oxide layer** has a **porous structure** immediately after the process. These pores can be used to absorb **dyes** or **pigments**.
 
• This allows **aluminium** products to be finished in a wide variety of **colors** while retaining the metallic texture, which is common in **consumer electronics** and **cookware**.
 
 
 
• **Electrical Properties**:
 
 
• While **aluminium** is an excellent conductor of electricity, **aluminium oxide** is an **insulator**.
 
• Therefore, **anodising** actually **decreases** the surface **electrical conductivity**, which can be useful in specific engineering applications where insulation is required.
 
 
 
• **Surface Hardness**:
 
 
• The **anodised layer** is significantly harder than the base metal. This provides excellent **abrasion resistance** and **wear resistance**, extending the lifespan of components used in **machinery** and **transportation**.
 
 
 
• **Adhesion**:
 
 
• The process provides a much better **adhesion** surface for **paints**, **primers**, and **glues** compared to bare metal, making it a critical pre-treatment step in many manufacturing workflows.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Common Applications**: **Anodised aluminium** is extensively used in **aerospace** for aircraft skins, **architecture** for window frames and roofs, and in **automotive** parts for its lightweight and rust-proof nature.
 
• **Maintenance**: Because the **oxide layer** is chemically stable, **anodised** surfaces require very low maintenance and are resistant to **UV radiation**, meaning the color does not fade easily over **years** of exposure.
 
• **Environmental Safety**: **Anodising** is considered an **environmentally safe** metal finishing process as it does not involve **heavy metals** like lead or cadmium, and the chemical by-products are often neutralized before disposal.
 
• **Comparison**: While **aluminium** forms a natural **oxide film** when exposed to **air**, this natural layer is very thin (approx **2-3 nanometers**). **Industrial anodising** can increase this thickness to **5 to 25 micrometers** or more, depending on the application.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: Advanced sunrise is due to scattering and delayed sunset is due to refraction.
Advanced sunrise and delayed sunset is due to atmospheric refraction.
Advanced sunrise and delayed sunset is due to scattering of light.
Advanced sunrise and delayed sunset is due to Earth’s rotation only.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Advanced sunrise and delayed sunset is due to atmospheric refraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction** is the phenomenon responsible for both **advanced sunrise** and **delayed sunset**. This occurs because the **Earth's atmosphere** is not uniform; it consists of layers with varying **optical densities** and **refractive indices**.
 
• **Advanced Sunrise**: The sun is visible to us about **2 minutes** before the actual sunrise. When the sun is slightly below the **horizon**, the light rays coming from it travel from rarer to denser layers of the atmosphere and bend toward the **normal**. To an observer on Earth, these rays appear to come from a position above the horizon. ***Hence, the statement regarding advanced sunrise being due to refraction is correct.***
 
• **Delayed Sunset**: Similarly, for the same reason of **atmospheric refraction**, the sun remains visible for about **2 minutes** after it has already crossed below the **horizon**. This creates the illusion that the sun is still present in the sky. ***Hence, the statement regarding delayed sunset being due to refraction is correct.***
 
• **Daylight Extension**: Because of these two effects, the total duration of **daylight** is increased by approximately **4 minutes** (2 minutes in the morning and 2 minutes in the evening).
 
• **Evaluation of Options**:
 
 
• Statement 1 suggests **scattering** causes advanced sunrise, which is scientifically inaccurate. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 correctly identifies **atmospheric refraction** as the cause for both events. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Statement 3 attributes the timing difference to the **scattering of light**, which actually causes the color changes, not the position shift. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 4 claims it is due to **Earth’s rotation** only; while rotation causes the day-night cycle, the timing discrepancy is an optical phenomenon. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Refraction**: As light travels from the vacuum of space into the **Earth's atmosphere**, it enters a denser medium. According to **Snell's Law**, light bends toward the normal as it moves into a medium with a higher **refractive index**. The air layers closer to the Earth's surface are denser than the upper layers, causing continuous bending of sunlight.
 
• **Apparent vs. Actual Position**: Due to **refraction**, the **apparent position** of the sun is slightly higher than its **actual position**. This effect is most pronounced when the sun is near the **horizon** (sunrise and sunset).
 
• **Scattering of Light**: It is important to distinguish refraction from **scattering**. Scattering (specifically **Rayleigh scattering**) is the process where gas molecules in the atmosphere redirect shorter wavelengths of light (blue/violet). This is why the sky appears blue and why the sun appears **reddish** during sunrise and sunset, as red light has a longer **wavelength** and is scattered the least.
 
• **Twinkling of Stars**: This is another classic example of **atmospheric refraction**. Starlight undergoes multiple refractions as it passes through different layers of the atmosphere with varying temperatures and densities, causing the **apparent position** of the star to fluctuate slightly, which we perceive as **twinkling**.
 
• **Flattening of the Sun**: **Atmospheric refraction** also causes the sun to appear **flattened** or oval-shaped during sunrise and sunset because the bottom edge of the sun is refracted more than the top edge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Refractive Index Variation**: The **refractive index** of air depends on its **temperature** and **pressure**. Colder air is denser and has a higher refractive index than warmer air.
 
• **Horizon Definition**: The **actual sunrise** is defined as the moment when the sun physically crosses the **horizon**. **Atmospheric refraction** allows us to see it before this physical event occurs.
 
• **Optical Illusions in Nature**: Other phenomena related to refraction include **mirages** in deserts or on hot roads, where light bends due to temperature gradients in the air near the ground.

• Due to this high reactivity, sodium is never found as a **pure element** in nature; it must be stored under **mineral oil** or **kerosene** to prevent reaction with **moisture** or **oxygen** in the air.

• **Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3)**, also known as **washing soda**, is vital in the manufacture of **glass**, **paper**, and **detergents**.
 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3)**, or **baking soda**, is widely used in the **food industry** and as a **fire extinguisher** component.
 
 
 
• **Biological Importance:**
 
 
• Sodium is an **essential electrolyte** for the human body. It is critical for maintaining **osmotic pressure**, **fluid balance**, and the **transmission of nerve impulses**.
 
• The **sodium-potassium pump** is a vital mechanism in **cell biology** that moves ions across **cell membranes**.

• **Statement B** identifies the type of reaction. questions.question: When a rocket is launched upward, the forces on it are ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unbalanced**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For a rocket to move upward from its launchpad, the forces acting on it must be **unbalanced**. According to **Newton's First Law of Motion**, an object at rest will stay at rest unless acted upon by an external **unbalanced force**.
 
• When a rocket's engines ignite, they produce an upward force known as **thrust**. For the rocket to lift off, this **thrust** must be greater than the downward force of **gravity** (the rocket's weight).
 
• The **net force** is the vector sum of all forces. In this case, **Net Force = Thrust - (Weight + Air Resistance)**. Since the rocket accelerates upward, the **net force** is positive and non-zero, making the forces **unbalanced**. ***Hence, the correct option is Unbalanced.***
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion** states that **Acceleration (a) = Net Force (F) / Mass (m)**. Without an **unbalanced force**, the **acceleration** would be **zero**, and the rocket would either remain stationary or move at a constant velocity.
 
• If the forces were **balanced**, the upward **thrust** would exactly equal the downward **gravity** and **drag**, resulting in no change in the rocket's state of motion. ***Hence, the option 'Balanced' is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion:** This law is the fundamental principle behind rocket **propulsion**. It states that for every **action**, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**. The rocket pushes **exhaust gases** downward at high **velocity** (action), and these gases push the rocket upward (reaction).
 
• **Thrust:** This is the mechanical force generated by the rocket's **propulsion system**. It depends on the **mass flow rate** of the exhaust and the **exit velocity** of the gases. To achieve **orbit**, engines must maintain high **thrust** levels for an extended **duration**.
 
• **Gravity:** Throughout the flight, **gravity** acts as a constant downward force. Its **magnitude** decreases slightly as the rocket moves further from **Earth's center**, but it remains a primary factor the rocket must overcome using **fuel** and **combustion**.
 
• **Air Resistance (Drag):** As the rocket travels through the **atmosphere**, air molecules collide with it, creating **friction** or **drag**. This force acts in the **opposite direction** of the rocket's motion and increases with **velocity** and **atmospheric density**.
 
• **Mass Variation:** Unlike many other vehicles, a rocket's **mass** changes significantly during flight because it consumes a massive amount of **propellant** (fuel and oxidizer). As **mass** decreases and **thrust** remains constant, the **acceleration** increases dramatically.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vector Quantities:** Force and acceleration are **vector quantities**, meaning they have both **magnitude** and **direction**. The direction of the **unbalanced force** determines the direction of the **acceleration**.
 
• **Inertia:** The tendency of the rocket to resist changes in its state of motion is called **inertia**, which is directly proportional to its **mass**. High **inertia** requires a larger **unbalanced force** to achieve the same **acceleration**.
 
• **Equilibrium:** An object is in **mechanical equilibrium** when the **sum of forces** is **zero** (balanced). A rocket sitting on a launchpad before ignition is in **static equilibrium**, where the **normal force** from the ground balances **gravity**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Sir **Isaac Newton** published these laws in his work **Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in **1687**, which laid the foundation for modern **aerospace engineering** and **physics**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an abiotic resistance for crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insects**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abiotic resistance** refers to a plant's ability to survive and grow under **non-living environmental stresses**. These factors are physical or chemical rather than biological.
 
• **Salinity** is an **abiotic factor** characterized by an **excessive concentration of salts** (like **Sodium Chloride**) in the soil. It affects the **osmotic potential** of the plant, making it difficult to absorb water. *Hence, this is an abiotic resistance factor.*
 
• **Heat** is a critical **abiotic stress** caused by **high temperatures** that exceed the optimal range for plant enzymes. It can lead to **protein denaturation** and **reduced photosynthetic efficiency**. *Hence, this is an abiotic resistance factor.*
 
• **Drought** is an **abiotic factor** resulting from a **prolonged shortage of water**. Plants develop resistance through mechanisms like **deep root systems**, **stomatal closure**, and **osmotic adjustment**. *Hence, this is an abiotic resistance factor.*
 
• **Insects** are **living organisms** (animals) that cause **biological damage** to crops through feeding, egg-laying, or by acting as **disease vectors**. Stresses caused by living entities are classified as **biotic stresses**, not abiotic. ***Hence, Insects is the correct answer as it is NOT an abiotic resistance factor.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biotic Stress in Crops**:
 
 
• This involves damage caused by **living organisms** such as **fungi**, **bacteria**, **viruses**, **nematodes**, **weeds**, and **insects**.
 
• Examples include the **Desert Locust** (pest), **Late Blight** in potatoes (fungal), and **Rice Tungro Virus**.
 
• Resistance is often achieved through **Biotechnology**, such as the development of **Bt Cotton** which produces a toxin to kill certain pests.
 
 
 
• **Abiotic Stress Factors**:
 
 
• These are **environmental conditions** that limit crop productivity. Besides salinity, heat, and drought, they include **frost/cold**, **flooding**, **radiation**, and **heavy metal toxicity** (like **Lead** or **Arsenic**).
 
• According to agricultural data, abiotic stresses are responsible for more than **50%** of the global **yield loss** in major crops like **wheat**, **rice**, and **maize**.
 
 
 
• **Plant Adaptations**:
 
 
• Plants respond to **abiotic stress** by producing **Heat Shock Proteins (HSPs)** or secondary metabolites like **proline** to maintain cellular stability.
 
• **Xerophytes** are specifically adapted to **drought**, while **Halophytes** are plants naturally resistant to **salinity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Food Security**: Developing **multi-stress resistant** varieties is essential for maintaining **global food security** in the face of **climate change**.
 
• **Measurement Units**: Soil **salinity** is often measured by **Electrical Conductivity (EC)**, while **drought** intensity is monitored using the **Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI)**.
 
• **Breeding Techniques**: Modern **Genome Editing** tools like **CRISPR-Cas9** are being used to enhance **abiotic resistance** in crops by targeting specific stress-responsive genes.
 
• **Classification**: It is important to distinguish between **Resistance** (ability to prevent the stress) and **Tolerance** (ability to endure the stress without significant yield loss).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of elements has the same number of neutrons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**B, C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The number of **neutrons** in an atom is calculated by subtracting the **atomic number (Z)** from the **mass number (A)**. The formula is: **Number of Neutrons = A - Z**.
 
• For **Boron (B)**, the most common isotope has an **atomic number** of **5** and a **mass number** of approximately **11**. Therefore, the number of neutrons is **11 - 5 = 6**.
 
• For **Carbon (C)**, the most common isotope (Carbon-12) has an **atomic number** of **6** and a **mass number** of **12**. Therefore, the number of neutrons is **12 - 6 = 6**.
 
• Comparing the two, both **Boron (B)** and **Carbon (C)** possess **6 neutrons** in their most stable forms. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• In contrast, for **Lithium (Li)**, the atomic number is **3** and the mass number is **7**, giving **4 neutrons**. For **Beryllium (Be)**, the atomic number is **4** and the mass number is **9**, giving **5 neutrons**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):** It represents the number of **protons** in the nucleus of an atom. It is unique to every element and determines its position in the **Modern Periodic Table**. For example, **Helium** has **2** protons, while **Lithium** has **3**.
 
• **Mass Number (A):** It is the total sum of **protons** and **neutrons** (collectively called nucleons) in the nucleus. It is usually denoted as a **whole number** in calculations. For instance, the mass number of **Beryllium** is **9**.
 
• **Isotones:** Elements or atoms that have the same number of **neutrons** but different **atomic numbers** and **mass numbers** are called **isotones**. In this question, **Boron-11** and **Carbon-12** are examples of isotones.
 
• **Isotopes:** These are atoms of the same element having the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers**. For example, **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-14** are isotopes of **Carbon**.
 
• **Isobars:** These are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same **mass number** but different **atomic numbers**. An example is **Argon-40** and **Calcium-40**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery of Neutrons:** The **neutron** was discovered by the British physicist **James Chadwick** in the year **1932**. It is a subatomic particle with **no net electric charge** and a mass slightly greater than that of a **proton**.
 
• **Elements Comparison:**
 
 
• **Helium (He):** Atomic Number **2**, Mass Number **4**, Neutrons = **2**.
 
• **Lithium (Li):** Atomic Number **3**, Mass Number **7**, Neutrons = **4**.
 
• **Beryllium (Be):** Atomic Number **4**, Mass Number **9**, Neutrons = **5**.
 
• **Boron (B):** Atomic Number **5**, Mass Number **11**, Neutrons = **6**.
 
• **Carbon (C):** Atomic Number **6**, Mass Number **12**, Neutrons = **6**.
 
 
 
• The distribution of electrons, protons, and neutrons determines the **chemical and physical properties** of the element. Neutrons play a critical role in the **stability** of the nucleus.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements about lysosomes is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the **Golgi apparatus**. They are often referred to as the "**suicidal bags**" of the cell.
 
• These organelles contain a wide variety of **hydrolytic enzymes** (**hydrolases**), such as **lipases**, **proteases**, and **carbohydrases**, which are optimally active at an **acidic pH**. These enzymes are responsible for digesting **carbohydrates**, **proteins**, **lipids**, and **nucleic acids**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The synthesis of **fats** (**lipids**) and **steroids** primarily takes place in the **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum** (**SER**), not in the lysosomes. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Protein synthesis** is the primary function of **ribosomes**, which may be found floating freely in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum** (**RER**). Lysosomes do not synthesize proteins; they degrade them. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Growth hormones** are signaling molecules produced by specialized **endocrine glands**, such as the **pituitary gland**. They are not contained or produced within lysosomes. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure and Discovery:** 
 
 
• **Lysosomes** were discovered by the Belgian cytologist **Christian de Duve** in **1955**.
 
• They are typically **spherical** in shape and are enclosed by a **single unit membrane** to prevent the powerful enzymes from leaking and destroying the rest of the cell.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Action:** 
 
 
• Lysosomes maintain an internal **acidic environment** (around **pH 4.5 to 5.0**) through **proton pumps** in their membranes that transport **H+ ions** from the cytosol.
 
• They are involved in **autophagy** (digesting the cell's own damaged organelles) and **heterophagy** (digesting external materials like bacteria or food particles taken in via **endocytosis**).
 
 
 
• **Types of Lysosomes:** 
 
 
• **Primary Lysosomes:** Newly formed vesicles from the **Golgi body** containing inactive enzymes.
 
• **Secondary Lysosomes:** Formed by the fusion of a primary lysosome with a **phagosome** or **food vacuole**; this is where active digestion occurs.
 
• **Residual Bodies:** Lysosomes containing undigested material that are eventually eliminated via **exocytosis**.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Significance:** 
 
 
• Malfunctioning of lysosomal enzymes can lead to **Lysosomal Storage Diseases** (**LSDs**), such as **Tay-Sachs disease** or **Gaucher's disease**, where undigested substances accumulate and damage tissues.
 
• They are highly abundant in **animal cells**, particularly in **White Blood Cells** (**leukocytes**) like **macrophages**, which utilize lysosomal enzymes to destroy pathogens.
 
 
</ul

__
 
• The analogy focuses on the **biological function** of specific substances in **plants**. Just as **Chlorophyll** is defined by its role as a **green pigment**, **Starch** is defined by its role as **energy storage**.
 
• **Starch** is a **polysaccharide** carbohydrate consisting of a large number of **glucose** units joined by **glycosidic bonds**. It is the primary way **autotrophic plants** store excess **energy** produced during **metabolism**.
 
• During the process of **photosynthesis**, plants synthesize **glucose**. Since glucose is soluble in **water** and can affect the **osmotic pressure** of cells, plants convert it into **insoluble starch** for long-term **storage** in organs like **roots**, **tubers**, and **seeds**.
 
• In the analogy, **Chlorophyll** is the substance that captures **light energy** from the **sun**, while **Starch** is the chemical form in which that **energy** is kept for later use, such as during the **night** or **dormant periods**.
 
• **Starch** is the most common **carbohydrate** in the human diet and is contained in large amounts in **staple foods** such as **potatoes**, **maize** (corn), **rice**, and **wheat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• It comprises two types of **molecules**: **Amylose** and **Amylopectin**.
 
• **Amylose** is a **linear** chain of glucose and makes up about **20% to 30%** of the structure, while **Amylopectin** is **highly branched** and makes up the remaining **70% to 80%**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Glycogen**:
 
 
• While **plants** use **starch** for **energy storage**, **animals** and **humans** use **glycogen**.
 
• **Glycogen** is stored primarily in the **liver** and **skeletal muscles** and is broken down into **glucose** when the body requires a quick **energy boost**.
 
 
 
• **Chlorophyll Characteristics**:
 
 
• It is located within the **thylakoid membranes** of the **chloroplasts**.
 
• The **central atom** in a **chlorophyll molecule** is **Magnesium (Mg)**. It absorbs **wavelengths** of light in the **blue** and **red** regions but reflects **green** light, which gives **plants** their characteristic color.
 
 
 
• **Biochemical Testing**:
 
 
• The presence of **starch** can be easily detected using **Iodine solution**. A **chemical reaction** occurs that turns the solution to a **blue-black color** if starch is present.
 
• This **test** is a fundamental experiment in **botany** and **biochemistry** to demonstrate the occurrence of **photosynthesis** in leaves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Carbohydrate Classification**: **Starch** belongs to the **complex carbohydrate** group because it is a **polymer** of **monosaccharides**. Unlike **simple sugars**, it provides **sustained energy** release.
 
• **Industrial Uses**: Beyond **nutrition**, starch is used in the **paper industry** for sizing, in the **textile industry** for stiffening fabrics, and as a **thickening agent** in the **food industry**.
 
• **Evolutionary Significance**: The ability of **plants** to store **energy** as **starch** allowed them to survive in **seasonal climates** where **sunlight** or **water** might be scarce for several **months** of the **year**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to reduce reverberations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Using sound-absorbent materials**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reverberation** is defined as the **persistence of sound** in an enclosed space after the original source of sound has stopped. It occurs due to **multiple reflections** of sound waves from surfaces like **walls**, **ceilings**, and **floors**.
 
• To reduce reverberation, the surfaces of the room or auditorium must be covered with **sound-absorbent materials**. These materials reduce the amount of reflected energy by converting sound energy into **heat energy** within the material. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Using **hard concrete floors** would actually increase reverberation because **concrete** is a rigid and non-porous material that reflects nearly all incident sound waves. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Removing furniture** increases the volume of open space and exposes more reflective surfaces. Items like **sofas**, **cushioned chairs**, and **wooden desks** act as obstacles and partial absorbers; removing them makes the room more "live" and increases the **reverberation time**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Marble walls** are highly polished, dense, and **hard surfaces**. They have a very low **absorption coefficient**, meaning they reflect sound waves very efficiently, which would lead to prolonged reverberation and potential echoes. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Commonly used **absorbent materials** include **compressed fiberboard**, **glass wool**, **heavy curtains**, and **carpets**. These are specifically designed with **porous structures** to trap sound waves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Absorption**: When sound waves strike **porous materials**, the air molecules vibrate inside the tiny pores. The **friction** between the air molecules and the walls of the pores converts the **vibrational energy** into **thermal energy**, thereby reducing the reflected sound.
 
• **Acoustic Panelling**: In **cinemas** and **concert halls**, walls are often covered with **perforated acoustic panels**. These panels have **small holes** that allow sound to enter and get trapped in the **insulating material** behind them.
 
• **Impact of Soft Furnishings**: Materials such as **draperies**, **upholstered seats**, and **wall-to-wall carpeting** are effective in residential and commercial settings to maintain **acoustic comfort** and prevent **speech unintelligibility**.
 
• **Absorption Coefficient**: This is a **numerical value** ranging from **0 to 1**. A value of **0** represents a perfect reflector (no absorption), while a value of **1** represents a perfect absorber. Materials like **open windows** have a coefficient of **1.0** as no sound is reflected back.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reverberation Time (RT)**: This is the **time duration** required for the sound pressure level to decrease by **60 decibels (dB)** after the source has stopped. This standard is often referred to as **RT60**.
 
• **Sabine's Formula**: The **reverberation time** is calculated using **Sabine's Equation**, which states that the time is **directly proportional** to the **volume** of the room and **inversely proportional** to the **total absorption** area.
 
• **Optimal Times**: Different environments require different **reverberation times**. For example, a **lecture hall** requires a low **RT** (around **0.5 to 1.0 seconds**) for **speech clarity**, whereas a **cathedral** or **concert hall** for **pipe organ music** may have an **RT** of over **2.0 seconds** to create a "full" sound.
 
• **Echo vs Reverberation**: An **echo** is a **distinct reflection** that reaches the ear at least **0.1 seconds** after the original sound. **Reverberation** is the **blending** of many reflections so close together that they cannot be distinguished as separate sounds.
</ul

questions.question: Which part in the ovule helps in guiding the pollen tube (carrying sperm nuclei) towards the female gamete?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Synergids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Synergids** are two specialized cells located at the **micropylar end** of the **embryo sac** in **angiosperms**. They are part of the **egg apparatus**, which also includes the **egg cell** (female gamete).
 
• The primary function of **synergids** is to guide the **pollen tube** toward the female gamete. This guidance is achieved through **chemotropic attraction**, where the synergids secrete specific chemical substances that direct the pollen tube's growth.
 
• Inside the synergids, there is a specialized cellular structure called the **filiform apparatus**. These are thick, finger-like projections of the cell wall that play a vital role in directing the **pollen tube** into the **embryo sac** and facilitating the release of **sperm nuclei**.
 
• During the process of fertilization, one of the **synergids** usually starts to degenerate before or upon the entry of the **pollen tube**, creating a passage for the male gametes to reach the egg cell and the central cell. ***Hence, the statement that synergids help in guiding the pollen tube is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Antipodal Cells**:
 
 
• These are a group of **three cells** located at the **chalazal end** (opposite to the micropyle) of the **embryo sac**.
 
• In most plants, their function is to provide **nutrition** to the developing **embryo sac**, although they typically degenerate before or shortly after **fertilization**.
 
 
 
• **Endosperm**:
 
 
• The **endosperm** is the nutritive tissue formed as a result of **triple fusion** (one male gamete fusing with **two polar nuclei**) during **double fertilization**.
 
• It is usually **triploid (3n)** and serves as a food source for the **embryo** during **seed development** and germination.
 
 
 
• **Style**:
 
 
• The **style** is the long, slender tube-like part of the **carpel** (or pistil) that connects the **stigma** to the **ovary**.
 
• While the **pollen tube** must grow through the tissues of the **style** to reach the **ovule**, the **style** itself does not provide the final chemical guidance into the **embryo sac**; that role belongs to the **synergids**.
 
 
 
• **Double Fertilization**:
 
 
• This is a characteristic feature of **flowering plants** (angiosperms) where **two male gametes** are released into the **embryo sac**.
 
• One male gamete fuses with the **egg cell** to form a **diploid zygote (2n)**, and the other fuses with the **central cell** containing **two polar nuclei** to form the **primary endosperm nucleus (PEN)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **embryo sac** in a typical angiosperm is an **8-nucleate, 7-celled** structure.
 
• The **micropyle** is the small opening in the **integuments** of the **ovule** through which the **pollen tube** usually enters.
 
• The **chemotropic signals** involved in guidance often include **calcium ions** and specific **proteins** secreted by the **filiform apparatus**.
</ul

questions.question: The tongue helps in digestion mainly by _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mixing food with saliva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **tongue** is a vital muscular organ located in the **oral cavity** (mouth) that functions as a primary accessory organ in the **digestive system**.
 
• One of its most important roles is **mixing food with saliva**. This process ensures that food is sufficiently moistened and lubricated for easy passage through the **esophagus**. ***Hence, the correct answer is mixing food with saliva.***
 
• The tongue facilitates the formation of a **bolus**, which is a small, rounded mass of chewed food. By manipulating the food against the **palate** and teeth, it prepares the food for **deglutition** (swallowing).
 
• It acts as a sensory organ equipped with **taste buds** located on various types of **papillae** (such as fungiform and circumvallate). These receptors detect **sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami** flavors, which triggers the brain to signal the stomach to begin producing **gastric juices**.
 
• During the process of **mastication** (chewing), the tongue constantly repositions food between the **teeth** to ensure it is ground efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical Digestion in the Mouth:**
 
 
• While the tongue mixes the food, the **salivary glands** (parotid, submandibular, and sublingual) secrete **saliva** containing the enzyme **salivary amylase** (also known as **ptyalin**).
 
• This enzyme initiates the chemical breakdown of complex **carbohydrates** (starch) into simpler sugars like **maltose**.
 
 
 
• **Anatomy of the Tongue:**
 
 
• The tongue is composed of **skeletal muscle**, allowing for voluntary control and highly flexible movements.
 
• It is anchored to the floor of the mouth by a vertical fold of mucous membrane called the **lingual frenulum**.
 
 
 
• **Misconceptions in Digestion:**
 
 
• The tongue does not **secrete digestive enzymes**; these are produced by the **salivary glands**, **stomach**, and **pancreas**.
 
• The **teeth**, not the tongue, are responsible for the mechanical action of **crushing food into smaller pieces**.
 
• The **absorption of nutrients** occurs predominantly in the **small intestine**, specifically through the **villi** and **microvilli** in the **jejunum** and **ileum**.
 
 
 
• **Non-Digestive Functions:**
 
 
• Beyond digestion, the tongue is essential for **phonation** (speech) and helps in cleaning the teeth by dislodging food particles after a meal.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: A train of length 282 m takes 12 seconds to pass over another train 248 m long coming from the opposite direction. If the speed of the first train is 68 km/hr, then find the speed of the second train.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 282 + 248 = 530 m

Relative speed = 530 ÷ 12 ≈ 44.17 m/s

Convert first train speed: 68 km/hr = 18.89 m/s

Second train speed = 44.17 − 18.89 ≈ 25.28 m/s

**∴ Answer = 91 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train = 282 m

Length of second train = 248 m

Time = 12 seconds

Speed of first train = 68 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Relative speed (opposite direction) = (sum of lengths) ÷ time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 282 + 248 = 530 m

⇒ Relative speed = 530 ÷ 12 ≈ 44.17 m/s

⇒ Convert 68 km/hr into m/s ⇒ 68 × 5/18 ≈ 18.89 m/s

⇒ Let speed of second train = v

⇒ Relative speed = 18.89 + v

⇒ 18.89 + v = 44.17

⇒ v ≈ 25.28 m/s

⇒ Convert into km/hr ⇒ 25.28 × 18/5 ≈ 91 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 91 km/hr.**

Relative Speed

Opposite direction ⇒ speeds are added.

Distance = sum of lengths when crossing.

Unit Conversion

km/hr to m/s ⇒ multiply by 5/18.

questions.question: If m and n are positive integers and (m – n) is an even number, then (m² – n²) will always be divisible by:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

m − n even ⇒ m and n have same parity (both even or both odd)

Then m + n is also even

m² − n² = (m − n)(m + n)

Even × Even = divisible by 4

**∴ Answer = 4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

m − n is even

m² − n² = (m − n)(m + n)

**Calculation:**

⇒ If m − n is even ⇒ m and n are both even or both odd

⇒ Case 1: m, n both even ⇒ m − n and m + n both even

⇒ Case 2: m, n both odd ⇒ m − n and m + n both even

⇒ So in all cases, both factors are even

⇒ Product = even × even

⇒ Hence divisible by 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

Parity Concept

Same parity numbers give even sum and difference.

Divisibility Rule

Product of two even numbers is always divisible by 4.

questions.question: In a right – angled ABC, right – angled at B, if tanA = (3)/(4), then find cosec A.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given tan A = 3/4, which represents the ratio of Perpendicular to Base.

The sides form a standard Pythagorean triplet of (3, 4, 5).

Thus, Perpendicular = 3, Base = 4, and Hypotenuse = 5.

We know that cosec A = Hypotenuse ÷ Perpendicular.

⇒ cosec A = 5/3

**∴ The correct answer is 5/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In a right-angled ΔABC, right-angled at B, tan A = 3/4

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

cosec A = Hypotenuse ÷ Perpendicular

 
 
 
 A A B C Base = 4x Perp = 3x Hypotenuse = 5x 

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan A = BC / AB = 3 / 4

⇒ Let Perpendicular BC = 3x and Base AB = 4x.

⇒ By Pythagoras Theorem in ΔABC:

⇒ AC² = AB² + BC²

⇒ AC² = (4x)² + (3x)²

⇒ AC² = 16x² + 9x²

⇒ AC² = 25x²

⇒ AC = √(25x²) = 5x

⇒ Now, cosec A = AC / BC

⇒ cosec A = 5x / 3x = 5/3

**∴ The correct answer is 5/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse | cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse | tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

Pythagorean Triplets

Standard integer combinations fulfilling the Pythagoras theorem include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Reciprocal Identities

cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ | sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ | cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ.

Work by (B + C) in 12 hrs = (15 − 10) × 12 = 60 units.

Remaining work = 270 − (165 + 60) = 45 units.

Time taken by B alone = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

If ‘A’ stands for ‘÷’, ‘B’ stands for ‘×’, ‘C’ stands for ‘+’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘−’, what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

 49 { B } 9 { D } 609 { A } 7 { C } 214 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7751840ca1840d12cadc428f84d30e2cdcd5e7f82d52a57de21f2404c58eed88.png] 

Decoding the given information:

 
 

 Alphabet
 A
 B
 C
 D
 
 
 
 

 Meaning
 ÷
 ×
 +
 −
 
 

Now, replacing the sign from left to right using BODMAS Rule, we get:

⇒ __**49 × 9**__ − __**609 ÷ 7**__ + 214 = ?

⇒ __**441**__ − 87 __**+ 214**__ = ?

⇒ __**655 − 87**__ = ?

⇒ 568

Hence, the correct option is **"Option 4"**.

questions.question: In April 2025, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) reduced the policy repo rate by 25 basis points, bringing it down to _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.00%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **first bi-monthly monetary policy** review for the financial year **2025-26**, held in **April 2025**, the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** decided to reduce the **policy repo rate**.
 
• The **MPC** implemented a reduction of **25 basis points (bps)**, which successfully brought the **repo rate** down from **6.25%** to **6.00%**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 6.00%.***
 
• The primary objective behind this rate cut is to stimulate **economic growth** by lowering the cost of borrowing for **commercial banks**, which in turn benefits **businesses** and **individual consumers**.
 
• This decision was taken by a majority vote within the **six-member committee**, assessing the prevailing **inflation** levels and the global **macroeconomic** environment.
 
• By adjusting the **repo rate**, the **RBI** manages the **liquidity** in the banking system, ensuring that **inflation** remains within the target range of **4% (+/- 2%)** while supporting **GDP growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Repo Rate (Repurchase Rate):**

 
 
• It is the rate at which the **Central Bank (RBI)** lends money to **commercial banks** against **government securities** to meet their short-term fund requirements.
 
• A decrease in the **repo rate** typically leads to cheaper **loans** (Home, Auto, Personal) for the general public, as **banks** pass on the benefit of lower costs to **borrowers**.
 
 
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate:**
 
 
• This is the rate at which the **RBI** borrows money from **commercial banks** within the country to absorb excess **liquidity** from the market.
 
• Usually, the **reverse repo rate** is lower than the **repo rate**, creating a **corridor** for interest rate movements.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a statutory body established under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, specifically through an amendment in **2016**.
 
• It consists of **6 members**: **3 members** from the **RBI** (including the **Governor** as the ex-officio **Chairperson**) and **3 external members** appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
 
 
• **Basis Points (bps):**
 
 
• In finance, **100 basis points** are equal to **1%**. Therefore, a **25 bps** cut represents a **0.25%** reduction in the interest rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact on Banking Sector:** When the **RBI** reduces the **repo rate**, banks often reduce the interest rates on **Fixed Deposits (FDs)** and **Savings Accounts**, which may impact the income of **senior citizens** and **savers**.
 
• **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) and Bank Rate:** These rates are typically adjusted in alignment with the **repo rate** changes. The **MSF** is the rate at which **banks** can borrow **overnight** from the **RBI** against their excess **SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio)** securities.
 
• **Stance of Policy:** The **MPC** also announces its **monetary policy stance**, such as **'accommodative'**, **'neutral'**, or **'withdrawal of accommodation'**, to signal future interest rate trajectories.
 
• **Inflation Target:** The **Government** and **RBI** have set a target for **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** inflation to ensure price stability, which is a key factor in deciding whether to hike or cut the **repo rate**.

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the **Similipal** region in **Odisha** was officially notified as India’s **107th National Park**, marking a significant milestone in India's conservation efforts.
 
• Located in the **Mayurbhanj district** of **Odisha**, this notification provides the area with the highest level of legal protection under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• While the region was already recognized as a **Wildlife Sanctuary** and a **Tiger Reserve**, the status of a **National Park** ensures stricter regulations regarding human activity and habitat preservation.
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** issued the final notification following the settlement of rights and boundary demarcations by the **State Government of Odisha**.
 
• Similipal is renowned for being the only natural habitat in the world for **Melanistic Tigers** (black tigers), and this upgraded status aims to further protect their unique genetic lineage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Similipal Biosphere Reserve:**

 
 
• It was formally designated as a **Tiger Reserve** in **1956** and became part of **Project Tiger** in **1973**.
 
• It was declared a **Biosphere Reserve** by the Government of India in **June 1994** and has been part of the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** since **2009**.
 
• The park derives its name from the **'Simul'** (red silk cotton) trees that are found in abundance in the region.
 
• Geographically, it features spectacular waterfalls such as **Barehipani** (one of India's highest) and **Joranda**.
 
 
 
• **National Parks in India:**
 
 
• National Parks are areas reserved for the improvement of wildlife where activities like **forestry, grazing, or cultivation** are not permitted.
 
• With the addition of Similipal, the total number of National Parks in India stands at **107** as of **2025**.
 
• The **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** empowers both the Central and State governments to declare areas as National Parks if they are of adequate ecological, faunal, floral, or geomorphological importance.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Hemis National Park**: Located in **Ladakh**, it is the **largest National Park** in India and is world-famous for its **Snow Leopards**.
 
• **Bhitarkanika National Park**: Also located in **Odisha** (Kendrapara district), it is famous for its **mangrove ecosystem** and **Saltwater Crocodiles**.
 
• **Ranthambore National Park**: Located in **Sawai Madhopur, Rajasthan**, it is one of the most famous **Tiger Reserves** in Northern India, known for its diurnal tigers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Flora and Fauna:** Similipal is home to over **1,000 species of plants**, including **94 species of orchids**. Besides tigers, it supports populations of **Asian Elephants**, **Gaur** (Indian Bison), and **Chausingha** (Four-horned Antelope).
 
• **Tribal Population:** The area is inhabited by several indigenous tribes, including the **Erenga Kharias** and the **Mankirdias**, who have lived in harmony with the forest for generations.
 
• **Conservation Challenges:** The region often faces threats from **forest fires** during the summer months and **poaching**, which the National Park status aims to mitigate through increased funding and administrative surveillance.

questions.question: By June 2025, to which stance did the Reserve Bank of India shift back after moving away from its accommodative policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neutral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, through its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, officially shifted its stance to **Neutral** by **June 2025**. This move signifies a departure from the previous "**withdrawal of accommodation**" stance that had been maintained to tackle post-pandemic inflationary pressures.
 
• A **Neutral** stance implies that the central bank is open to moving interest rates in either direction—increasing or decreasing—depending on the evolving **macroeconomic data**, particularly **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** inflation and **GDP growth** trends.
 
• The transition away from an **Accommodative** policy began in **2022** as the **RBI** raised the **Repo Rate** to curb **Retail Inflation**. By mid-**2025**, the stabilization of inflation within the target band of **4% (+/- 2%)** prompted the shift back to **Neutral**.
 
• The **MPC**, led by the **Governor of the RBI**, evaluates various domestic and global factors before deciding on the stance. The shift to **Neutral** indicates that the **policy rates** are currently aligned with the objective of achieving the inflation target while supporting economic expansion.
 
• This policy change provides the **RBI** with greater flexibility to respond to global economic shocks or shifts in **Liquidity** conditions within the Indian banking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Monetary Policy Stances:**
 
 
• **Accommodative Stance:** This is adopted when the **RBI** is prepared to expand the **money supply** and lower **interest rates** to boost economic growth. It was notably used during the **COVID-19 pandemic** to provide **liquidity support**.
 
• **Neutral Stance:** Under this, the **central bank** keeps its options open. It neither commits to a rate cut nor a rate hike, allowing the **Repo Rate** to be adjusted based on real-time **economic indicators**.
 
• **Hawkish Stance:** This indicates a priority to control **inflation**. The central bank is likely to increase **interest rates** to reduce the money supply and cool down an overheating economy.
 
• **Dovish Stance:** This is the opposite of Hawkish, where the focus is on low-interest rates to encourage **borrowing** and **investment**, often at the risk of higher inflation.
 
 
 
• **The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member** statutory body constituted under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** (specifically **Section 45ZB**).
 
• It consists of **three internal members** from the **RBI** and **three external members** appointed by the **Central Government**.
 
• The committee meets at least **four times a year** (usually **bi-monthly**) to determine the **Policy Repo Rate** required to achieve the **inflation target**.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Targeting Framework:**
 
 
• The **Government of India**, in consultation with the **RBI**, sets a **flexible inflation target**. Currently, the target is **4%** with an upper tolerance limit of **6%** and a lower tolerance limit of **2%**.
 
• The primary tool used to manage this is the **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)**, which includes the **Repo Rate** and the **Reverse Repo Rate** (or the **Standing Deposit Facility**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Repo Rate:** The rate at which the **RBI** lends money to **commercial banks** in the event of any shortfall of funds. It is used to control **inflation**.
 
• **Withdrawal of Accommodation:** A transitional stance where the **RBI** gradually removes the **excess liquidity** pumped into the system during an **Accommodative** phase.
 
• **Impact on Consumers:** A shift to a **Neutral** stance often signals a peak in the **interest rate cycle**, suggesting that **EMIs** on home and auto loans may stabilize or eventually decrease if a rate cut follows.
</ul

questions.question: Which Ministry gave the idea of a common board for class 10 and 12 in seven states?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Education** (formerly known as the Ministry of Human Resource Development) has proposed the idea of a common assessment framework to bring **uniformity** across different state and central boards for **Class 10 and 12**.
 
• This initiative is primarily driven through the establishment of **PARAKH** (Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development), which acts as a **national assessment center**.
 
• The primary objective of this move by the **Ministry of Education** is to address the **disparity in evaluation** and marking schemes among various boards, which often affects students during college admissions in **Higher Education Institutions**.
 
• By proposing a common platform or "common board" guidelines for assessment, the ministry aims to ensure that **equivalence** is maintained between **State Boards**, **CBSE**, and **ICSE**.
 
• This reform was discussed in series of workshops involving representatives from various states to create a **benchmark** for student assessment that aligns with global standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**:
 
 
• The **NEP 2020** is the foundational document that recommended the setting up of a **standard-setting body** to guide school boards on assessment patterns.
 
• It emphasizes moving away from **rote learning** and towards **competency-based assessment** for **Class 10 and 12** students.
 
 
 
• **PARAKH (National Assessment Centre)**:
 
 
• Launched in **2023**, **PARAKH** is an unit under the **NCERT** (National Council of Educational Research and Training).
 
• It is tasked with setting **norms, standards, and guidelines** for student assessment and evaluation for all recognized school boards in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Diversity of Boards**:
 
 
• India currently has more than **60 different school boards**, each following its own syllabus and grading system.
 
• The **Ministry of Education** aims to bridge the gap between these boards to provide **equal opportunities** to students from rural and urban areas regardless of their board affiliation.
 
 
 
• **Equivalence of Certification**:
 
 
• A major focus of the **Ministry of Education** is to ensure that the difficulty level of exams and the **grading rigor** are comparable across all states, preventing "grade inflation" in specific regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Focus on Seven States**: The initial phase of discussing the common assessment framework involved deep consultation with various states to pilot the **standardization** of question papers and evaluation methods.
 
• **Holistic Progress Card (HPC)**: As part of these reforms, the **Ministry of Education** introduced the **360-degree Holistic Progress Card**, which tracks a student's **cognitive, affective, and psychomotor** domains instead of just marks.
 
• **Impact on Admissions**: Standardizing **Class 12** marks is crucial because many **central universities** and competitive exams rely on board percentages for eligibility or merit ranking.
 
• **Implementation Agency**: While the idea came from the **Ministry of Education**, the technical execution is supported by **NCERT** and international assessment experts to ensure **validity and reliability** of the new system.

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the district of **Nuapada** achieved the significant milestone of being officially declared the **first single-use plastic (SUP)–free district** in the state of **Odisha**.
 
• The declaration was the culmination of a rigorous and sustained campaign led by the **District Administration** to eliminate the usage of prohibited plastic items across both **urban and rural areas**.
 
• Success was achieved through the effective implementation of the **Plastic Waste Management Rules**, which included **strict enforcement**, regular **raids on wholesalers**, and the promotion of sustainable alternatives.
 
• The initiative involved widespread **community participation**, where local **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** and **Panchayati Raj Institutions** were empowered to monitor and report the use of **Single-Use Plastics**.
 
• To support the transition, the district set up several **Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs)** to ensure that plastic waste already in circulation was collected and processed efficiently. ***Hence, the correct answer is Nuapada.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Single-Use Plastic (SUP):**
 
 
• **Single-use plastics** refer to plastic items that are intended to be used only **once** for the same purpose before being **disposed of** or recycled.
 
• These items, such as **plastic straws**, **stirrers**, **polythene bags**, and **plastic cutlery**, are major contributors to **environmental pollution** as they do not biodegrade.
 
 
 
• **Plastic Ban in Odisha:**
 
 
• The **Government of Odisha** has been a pioneer in environmental conservation, having initially banned plastic in **six major cities** (Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Berhampur, Sambalpur, Rourkela, and Puri) on **Gandhi Jayanti** in **2018**.
 
• The statewide ban aligns with the **National Ban** on identified SUP items introduced by the **Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** which came into effect on **July 1, 2022**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Plastic waste is a significant threat to **marine life** and **soil fertility** in **Odisha**, particularly affecting sensitive zones like **Chilika Lake** and the **Bhitarkanika Mangroves**.
 
• By becoming **SUP-free**, districts like **Nuapada** help in reducing the **carbon footprint** and preventing the clogging of **drainage systems** during the monsoon.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **District Context:** While **Nuapada** took the lead in **2025**, other districts such as **Bargarh**, **Rayagada**, and **Kalahandi** have also been actively pursuing **waste management** protocols to achieve similar status.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The enforcement is carried out under the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**, where violators can face heavy **fines** or even **imprisonment** for non-compliance with plastic waste regulations.
 
• **Alternatives Promoted:** As part of the **SUP-free** movement, the government has encouraged the use of **cloth bags**, **jute products**, and leaf-based plates (**Sal leaves**), which are traditional to **Odisha's culture** and support local **artisans**.
 
• **Role of SPCB:** The **State Pollution Control Board (SPCB)** provides technical guidance and monitors the **air and water quality** improvements resulting from reduced plastic incineration and littering.
